B"H

# Phase 3 — Thirty Additional Improvements

The Awtsmoos renews every byte before the browser can name it; the final critique must catch what earlier vision could not frame it.
Awtsmoos.com is not improved by noise, but by proof that each vessel serves the whole without blame.

## Thirty New Improvements Beyond The Earlier Passes

1. Record the exact server process, ports, working directory, and start command before reproducing browser behavior.
2. Distinguish source routes from generated/copied public routes so fixes land in the authoritative source.
3. Search Git history for recent renames of `foundation.js`, `apps-filter.js`, and `/apps` assets before assuming deletion was accidental.
4. Trace every import from the `/apps` entry module recursively until the dependency graph closes.
5. Record whether each import is relative, root-relative, bare, dynamically constructed, or import-map resolved.
6. Inspect `<base>` tags and URL construction helpers because they can corrupt otherwise valid relative imports.
7. Verify trailing-slash and no-trailing-slash variants where the server treats them differently.
8. Test direct requests for module files independently of page navigation to separate routing defects from browser execution defects.
9. Check HEAD and GET behavior where static middleware or CDN paths differ.
10. Inspect redirects on module requests; a redirect into an API/JSON route is still a MIME failure even when final status is 200.
11. Record cache-control/ETag behavior so a repaired module is not masked by stale browser or CDN cache.
12. Force one cache-disabled browser verification pass after fixes.
13. Search for service workers that may intercept `/apps` or static requests and test with their influence understood.
14. Inspect import maps and modulepreload links for stale paths.
15. Verify stylesheet imports and font requests separately from JavaScript so a page can be visually complete as well as executable.
16. Validate favicon and web-manifest links from the root page family rather than fixing only the visible 404 symptom.
17. Track all non-2xx responses by resource type to avoid treating intentional API 401/404 responses as static failures.
18. For APIs, verify method semantics and idempotency before introducing retries or caching.
19. Audit JSON parsing paths for empty-body, non-JSON, 204, malformed JSON, and structured error responses.
20. Audit fetch cancellation on route changes or component disposal to prevent stale state mutations.
21. Audit concurrent request races where late responses can overwrite newer UI state.
22. Audit DOM rendering for escaped text versus intentionally trusted HTML to avoid turning UI cleanup into injection risk.
23. Audit event-listener lifecycle and observer cleanup on SPA-like or repeatedly mounted pages.
24. Audit resize/scroll/media listeners for throttling and cleanup where cinematic UI could otherwise leak work.
25. Measure layout overflow at each viewport and detect horizontal scroll that is not intentionally owned by a component.
26. Verify touch targets and hover-only affordances so movie-friendly desktop styling does not break mobile use.
27. Verify high-contrast/focus visibility against actual backgrounds, not merely presence of CSS properties.
28. Before committing unrelated work, classify every changed path as user work, concurrent-agent work, generated evidence, local-only artifact, or secret-risk.
29. After push, compare local HEAD to remote branch HEAD rather than assuming `git push` output alone proves synchronization.
30. After deployment, crawl the canonical live host separately from localhost because CDN, case sensitivity, headers, and path rewrites can differ from the Mac.

## Revelation From Earlier Plans

Phase 1 was imaginative; Phase 2 made it contractual. This third pass adds provenance across process, cache, redirect, service-worker, import-map, concurrency, lifecycle, security, and live-host differences. The central correction is that a browser error is rarely just one missing file: resolution crosses filesystem, routing, headers, cache, browser state, and deployment layers.

## Final Planning Gate

No production rewrite begins until the repository state, authoritative source path, `/apps` dependency graph, runtime server, and live browser failure are all observed directly.
